thesis_summary.thesis: A. O. Smith Corporation (AOS) is a global manufacturer of residential and commercial water heaters, boilers, heat pumps, tanks, and water treatment products. **[Fact]** The company reports two segments: **North America** (~78% of 2025 net sales) and **Rest of World** (primarily China, India, and Europe). **[Fact]** FY2025 consolidated net sales were **$3.83 billion** (flat versus $3.82 billion in 2024), net earnings **$546.2 million**, and free cash flow **$546.0 million**. **[Fact]** North America segment earnings were **$727.9 million** on **$2.98 billion** of sales (24.4% margin); Rest of World earned **$76.4 million** on **$880.4 million** of sales (8.7% margin). The company sells through roughly **800** independent wholesale plumbing distributors plus national retail and maintenance channels under brands including A. O. Smith, State, and Lochinvar.
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: The market may treat AOS as a mature, housing-cyclical name and underweight its pricing power and capital return. **[Fact]** Gross margin rose to **38.8%** in 2025 from **38.1%** in 2024 on early-year pricing actions and higher North America boiler mix. **[Fact]** Share count fell from **151.0 million** diluted shares in 2023 to **141.9 million** in 2025 while the company repurchased **5.9 million** shares for **$400.8 million** in 2025. **[Inference]** Generalists may anchor on flat revenue and Q1 2026 earnings softness (diluted EPS **$0.85** versus **$0.95** in Q1 2025) and miss that owner cash is growing through margin, buybacks, and lower capital spending after 2024 capacity projects. There is no dated catalyst; the inefficiency is **descriptive** (quality compounder near fair price), not an equity yield curve setup.
